title: The Mandate of Heaven and China's dynastic cycle

explain.say: Imagine a leader being told: you may rule only while you rule well. Ancient Chinese thinkers called this the Mandate of Heaven, which means permission from Heaven to rule. The circle shows how dynasties, ruling families, rose and fell again and again.

explain.say: Start at the crown. The Zhou family used this idea around 1046 BCE, when they overthrew the Shang. They said the Shang had lost Heaven's favour, so Heaven chose them. Can you see why a new ruler liked this idea?

explain.say: See the fire? A rebellion ends one dynasty and begins the next, from the Han to the Ming. Excellent thinking! Historians add that real life was messier than a neat circle. Wow: China's last dynasty, the Qing, ended in 1912, after over 2,000 years of emperors.

faq.q: What is the Mandate of Heaven?
faq.a: It is an ancient Chinese idea that Heaven lets a ruler govern only while they rule fairly and well. If they rule badly, Heaven can take that right away and give it to someone else.
asks: What does Mandate of Heaven mean?

faq.q: Why did Chinese dynasties grow weak?
faq.a: Common reasons were heavy taxes, corrupt officials, quarrels at court, and costly wars or building projects. Over time these made people unhappy and the government poorer.

faq.q: Why were floods seen as a warning?
faq.a: People believed a good ruler kept harmony between Heaven and Earth. So floods, droughts or earthquakes could look like signs that the ruler had lost Heaven's favour.
asks: Why did disasters matter to emperors?

faq.q: Who used the Mandate of Heaven first?
faq.a: The Zhou dynasty, who overthrew the Shang around 1046 BCE, are the first known to use it, to explain why their rule was right.
asks: Which dynasty started the Mandate of Heaven?

faq.a: It is the pattern historians see in Chinese history: a dynasty rises, grows strong, weakens, faces disasters and rebellion, and is replaced. It is a helpful model, not an exact rule.
asks: How did dynasties rise and fall?

facts: The Zhou dynasty, from about 1046 BCE, is the first known to use the Mandate of Heaven.
China's last imperial dynasty, the Qing, ended in 1912.

quiz.say: According to the Mandate of Heaven, when could a ruler lose the right to rule?
quiz.show: When could a ruler lose the Mandate?
quiz.why: The idea was that Heaven supports only fair and good rulers.

wrong.1: Age had nothing to do with it; behaviour did.
wrong.2: The whole point was that the Mandate could be lost.

quiz.say: Which dynasty first used the Mandate of Heaven?
quiz.show: Who first used the Mandate of Heaven?
quiz.why: The Zhou used it around 1046 BCE to explain replacing the Shang.

wrong.1: The Qing was the last dynasty, ending in 1912.
wrong.2: The Ming ruled from 1368 to 1644, much later.
